# The Window

The window framed a perfect square of blue. Not the deep blue of evening, nor the pale blue of early morning, but the solid, dependable blue of mid-afternoon. Sarah stood watching it, her fingers tracing invisible patterns on the glass.

Three floors below, the city continued its relentless rhythm. People moved in currents, flowing around obstacles, merging at intersections, dispersing into side streets. From this height, they seemed less like individuals and more like cells in a larger organism.

"You've been standing there for twenty minutes," Michael said from behind her.

Sarah didn't turn. "I'm trying to understand something."

"What?"

"I'm not sure yet."

Michael sighed and returned to his desk. The sound of his keyboard filled the apartment – a staccato counterpoint to the muffled city noise.

Sarah pressed her forehead against the glass. It was cool despite the summer heat. The building across the street mirrored their own – identical windows, identical lives playing out in parallel. In one, a man watered plants lined along his windowsill. In another, a child pressed colored paper to the glass.

"Do you ever wonder about them?" Sarah asked.

The typing paused. "About who?"

"The people in the other windows. Do you think they look over here too?"

"I suppose some do."

Sarah nodded. "I saw the woman in 5B crying yesterday. She stood right where I'm standing now, but she didn't seem to care who might see."

Michael's chair creaked as he turned. "Maybe she wanted to be seen."

"Maybe." Sarah's breath fogged the glass. She drew a small spiral in it with her fingertip. "Or maybe she thought she was alone."

"No one's ever really alone in the city."

"That's what makes it so lonely."

The blue of the sky was changing now, imperceptibly shifting toward evening. Soon the windows across the street would light up one by one, like stars appearing in reverse. Sarah would watch them all, these parallel lives, these strangers connected by nothing more than proximity and glass.

She wondered which ones were watching her.
